whatChanged.theDiagnosis: `composeBaseFactsSitus` (hauska-map `api/_lib/pe-record-to-facets.ts`) licenses the city-limits city only when the RECORD-SERVED `situsCity` cell reads `absent-verified`. On the four failing subjects the retrieval reader serves `situsCity`/`situsZip`/`situsState` as `legacy-transitional` (the wire's own `recordRailStates`), so that branch never ran — while `baseFacts.situsCity` carried the same declared `absent-verified` verdict from the bake and the served `cityLimitsFact` named the incorporated city. The licence's condition was right and its EVIDENCE PATH was wrong.
whatChanged.theLicence: Accept the PAYLOAD's own declaration, whichever path served it — chosen over cutting the three situs rails over to the record path, which is a ledger decision this lane does not own (and which is the only alternative that would make the live surface green without this change). A city is named only when BOTH hold: (1) the payload's situs city is a DECLARED `absent-verified` absence — a bare null, `refused`, `lookup-failed` or `not-applicable` licenses nothing, because the roll's silence is not evidence it has no city; (2) the payload's own served `cityLimitsFact` is `incorporated` AND names a city. A readable roll city is never replaced. The city it does name is stamped `situsCityBasis: "city-limits"`.
mapImplementation: api/_lib/pe-property-atoms.ts — `applyCityLimitsSitusLicence`, applied at the ONE point every served facets payload passes through and AFTER `applyRecordPatch`, so the licence reads the same `cityLimitsFact` the customer reads.
src/lib/baked-facets.ts — the baked card model carries the composer module's own sentence (`situsCityLimitsNote`) for a city-limits city.
src/browse/InspectCard.tsx — the row renders that note on the card face, so a jurisdiction city cannot read as the roll's mailing city (dispatch item 2).
ldtImplementation: src/lib/situsCompose.ts — `resolveSitusCity` decides the label's city and returns the basis it used; the declared-absence reader reads `verdict ?? status` in the order the probe reads it.

src/lib/smartSiteStub.ts — the city comes from the licence, not from a `typeof === "string"` test (the defect shape: `{status:"absent", verdict:"absent-verified"}` became null); new optional `cityLimitsFact` input.

src/routes/propertyExplorer.ts — `assembleStubBody` reads the city-limits determination ONLY for the declared-absence shape, so a stub whose payload states its own roll city reads nothing extra and is byte-identical.

probeInstrument.whatChanged: `extractFacets` now carries `situsCityBasis`; `addressCarriesLedgerLine` reads it to attribute the city it grades; a NEW falsifier FAILs where a payload claims a city-limits city its own `cityLimitsFact` does not license (the claim is not licensed by an `unincorporated` or differently-named answer, so the row can no longer be satisfied by a payload asserting a jurisdiction city on no authority); the X2-address defect text now includes "or names a city-limits city its own facts do not license".

p331Pin.status: P-331 MERGED ON BOTH MAINS during this lane (hauska-map #425, legacy-design-tools #725). Checked three times rather than assumed once: early = map half only (so the rule was NAMED); then #725 landed; final = both halves, and the two copies of the check are byte-identical (sha256 b2755e6e / 33941 bytes before this lane's header correction, 7bbbab6e / 34654 bytes after).
p331Pin.whatLandedInThisCommit: The declarations a row reads, under the same names on both sides: `SitusCityBasis` (map `src/lib/situs-address.ts`; LDT `situsCompose.ts`), `DECLARED_ABSENCE_VERDICT` and `CITY_LIMITS_INCORPORATED_STATUS` beside each. In hauska-map this also COLLAPSED two duplicate copies of the basis vocabulary (`pe-record-to-facets.ts`'s own narrower `SitusCityBasis` and `atom-chain-to-facets.ts`'s inline union) into the one declaration plus imports — the same disease P-331 exists to catch, one level down (three spellings of two words in one repo).
p331Pin.whatIsHeldAndWhy: The three ROWS. A row reads the SIBLING'S MAIN, so rows shipped in this pair of PRs exit 2 (REFUSE — never a pass, but a required check) on BOTH PRs before either merges and on whichever merges first after that. That is a red no single merge can clear, i.e. the dead gate DEV_PROCESS names. The two-landings rule is now stated in the check's own header in both repos (identical bytes), replacing the stale text that said the sibling's main had no copy of the file — true when written, false when read.
p331Pin.theThirdCopy: The probe's model of the rule (doc_repo `scripts/surface-probe.mjs`) is a THIRD repository's copy, outside the pair P-331 can read: NAMED, not pinned, and said so in both the check's header and the licence's comments.

revisionOfMyOwnEarlierConclusion.whatIClaimedAtCommitCdbee43: That P-331 was half-merged and the three copies of the rule were therefore NAMED, NOT PINNED, with the rows deferred to a handover.
revisionOfMyOwnEarlierConclusion.whatIsTrue: Both halves merged while this lane ran, so the pin became BUILDABLE — deferring on an unmerged-half argument would have been a stale reason within hours. The rows are still held, but on a different and measured reason (the sibling-main read makes them unmergeable-red in this pair of PRs), and the declarations that a row needs are landed rather than promised.
revisionOfMyOwnEarlierConclusion.howItWasCorrected: The lane's comments in both repos, the check's header (both byte-identical copies) and both PR bodies were corrected to the final state; CP1's `crossRepoPins` field was rewritten twice, the second time after measuring the merge, and no artifact is left claiming a status that was true only when written.
revisionOfMyOwnEarlierConclusion.whyThisMatters: A pin's whole value is that its status is a reading, not a memory. A comment that says "not merged" about a merged half is worse than no comment: it is the drift P-331 exists to catch, written into the file P-331 protects.
